claim: Technical specs for Naxos cheeses: graviera min 80% cow's milk, arseniko sheep+goat aged >=3 months, xinomizithra fresh goat cheese eaten within days.
quote: Graviera Naxou: Cow's milk (minimum 80%), sheep's and goat's milk (maximum 20%), aging at least three months. Xynomyzithra: rich and creamy with a slightly sour aftertaste which resembles yoghurt.

claim: Graviera Naxou is a PDO cheese, originally registered with the EU on 21 June 1996.
quote: Original EU Registration: 21 June 1996. Class: 1.3 Cheeses. Protected Designation of Origin (PDO). Country of Origin: Greece.

claim: Arseniko Naxou is a PDO cheese, originally registered with the EU on 20 January 2020.
quote: Original EU registration on 20 January 2020. Cheese product (Class 1.3) with Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) status from Greece.

claim: Axiotissa requires a reservation 3-4 days in advance in high season; area-by-area restaurant picks for Naxos.
quote: Axiotissa (Kastraki): Modern Greek, $$. Highly acclaimed; reservation required 3-4 days advance.

claim: 2026 Naxos panigiria calendar with dates and villages, food served, 5-10 EUR donation, and practical advice for the 15 August Filoti festival.
quote: the food is consistently local: lamb on the spit, baked fish, fava, local cheeses (Naxos kefalotyri and arseniko are both AOC), and Naxos wine in carafes

claim: Overview of Naxian products: male/female cheese naming, ladotyri, krasotyri, touloumisio, zamboni cured pork, ~100,000 sheep/goats vs ~4,000 cattle, Naxos not a major wine region.
quote: Naxos maintains approximately 100,000 sheep/goats and 4,000 cattle. Zamboni is a firm, salted, and delicious cured pork served thinly sliced. Ladotyri: Matured cheese submerged in olive oil for three months before consumption.

claim: Arseniko Naxou is a matured hard cheese of non-pasteurised goat and sheep milk produced in the Municipality of Naxos and the Small Cyclades.
quote: Arseniko Naxou is a matured, hard cheese traditionally made of non-pasteurised goat and sheep milk, and is produced in many areas of the Municipality of Naxos and the Small Cyclades.

claim: Patata Naxou PGI registered 1 December 2011; spring harvest end of May to early July, autumn planting Aug-Sep; varieties Liseta, Spunta, Marfona, Vivaldi, Alaska.
quote: Registration Year: 2011 (December 1st). Potato Varieties: Liseta, Spunta, Marfona, Vivaldi, and Alaska. The flesh is yellowish-white with an earthy and distinctive flavour.

claim: Naxos potato history (offered to King Otto in 1841), sowing mid-Feb to early March, harvest late May to first ten days of July, Potato Festival at Agia Anna in July/August.
quote: For the spring crop, which is the most widespread on Naxos, sowing takes place from mid-February to early March. The harvest begins in late May and usually ends in the first ten days of July.

claim: EAS Naxos founded 1926, 26 member cooperatives, ~3,274 farmers, processes ~12,000 t milk/yr (>70% of island production), Glinado dairy from 1985, milk cheesed within 8 hours.
quote: The operation processes about 12.000 tons per year, over 70% of the island's milk production... cheese is made, no later than 8 hours after collection.

claim: EAS Naxos product range (Graviera Naxou PDO, Patata Naxou PGI), shop hours on the Chora seafront and dairy plant hours at Agia Eirini/Glinado; no public factory tour advertised.
quote: Grocery Store (Naxos Chora seafront) Hours: Mon-Sat 8:00-21:00, Sun 8:00-14:30. Milk Processing Plant (Agia Eirini, Glinado) Hours: Mon-Sat 8:30-14:30.

claim: Vallindras distillery in Halki established 1896, now largely a museum with tasting and shop; reachable on bus lines 2, 6 and 7 from Chora.
quote: The distillery was established in 1896 and was managed by the Vallindras family... Public transport: Bus lines 2, 6, and 7 connect Chora to Halki.

claim: Vallindras sits on Halki's main square, distilling kitron the same way since 1896, making three varieties plus a spice-infused liqueur.
quote: The Vallindras Distillery on Halki's main square has been distilling the kitron liqueur in the same way since 1896.

claim: Promponas distillery operating since 1915; citron varieties and ABVs (White Special 40%, Orange 40%, White 30%, Green 30%); three guided tour formats.
quote: White Citron Special: 40%; Orange Citron: 40%; White Citron: 30%; Green Citron: 30%.

claim: Promponas kitron distillery and wine tasting tour: EUR 65 adult, EUR 30 age 12-17, free under 12; 1h30; sessions at 10:00/12:00/14:00; max 10 people; 48h free cancellation; at Loukaki.
quote: Price: EUR 65 per adult (18+); EUR 30 for children (12-17); free for children under 12. Duration: 1 hour 30 minutes. Three daily sessions available (10:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 2:00 PM).

claim: Perivoli Naxian Farm cooking lesson and farm tour at Melanes: EUR 100 per person, 4h15, groups to 25, free cancellation to 24h, includes wood-fire cooking of Naxian dishes and lunch.
quote: Duration: 4 hours 15 minutes. Price: EUR 100 per person. Farm & Location: Perivoli Naxian Farm Experience, Melanes, Naxos.

claim: Saint Anna Winery at Kato Potamia opens Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00; tour includes a 9th-century Byzantine church, winery tour and tasting with local pairings; prices not published online.
quote: Opening Hours: Monday - Saturday, 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM. Location: Kato Potamia, Naxos Island.

claim: Saint Anna Winery founded 2016 by Emmanuel Petrakis, building on a family winemaking tradition dating to 1940; a 9th-century Saint Anna chapel stands on the property.
quote: Established in 2016 by Emmanuel Petrakis, who built upon his family's winemaking tradition dating back to 1940.

claim: Naxos produces 35 to 40 tons of honey annually, mostly thyme, with heather and spring-flower varieties.
quote: 35 to 40 tons produced annually, with thyme honey comprising the largest portion. Secondary varieties include heather and spring flower honey.

claim: Nature & Art is based in Halki, Naxos, with hives at Moni and Kinidaros producing thyme, heather and flower honey plus bee products.
quote: The bee colonies are situated in the villages of Moni and Kinidaros in central Naxos... The business is based in Halkio, Naxos, Greece.

claim: Naxia Gi in Halki sells locally produced honey, bee products, spices, teas and herbs.
quote: Naxia Gi - Honey, Spices, Herbs And Much More...

claim: Zamponi is cured pork leg coated in salt, pepper and cinnamon then kept in coarse salt for about six months; served thinly sliced; Apiranthos tradition ties slaughter to northerly winds.
quote: the pig should be slaughtered when northerly winds blow because only then is the meat drained properly... the leg receives a coating of salt, pepper, and cinnamon, then sits in a chest covered with coarse salt for approximately six months.

claim: 2026 Naxos restaurant roundup: Axiotissa (Kastraki), Stou Lefteri and Amorginos (Apeiranthos), Stou Vasilarakiou (Kinidaros), O Vassilis, Platia (Galini), To Gefyraki (Danakos), Apanemi and Alos (Moutsouna), Stelida, Petrino Beach, Naxos Apothecary, with signature dishes and official links.
quote: Axiotissa - Location: Kastraki - Known for: Slow-cooked lamb with garlic and kefalotyri, rooster in tomato sauce with linguine, fried potatoes, seafood - Website: axiotissa.com

claim: Naxos restaurants grouped by area with price bands and per-restaurant reservation guidance (Tortuga, Nissaki, Rotonda advance booking; Maro's, Paradiso, Peppermint walk-in; To Spitiko Galaktoboureko cash only and sells out).
quote: To Spitiko Galaktoboureko (Chalki) ($) - Reservations: Cash only, arrive early (sells out).

claim: Restaurant picks with price bands, reservation notes and official sites: Doukato (gouna, fried cheese), Barozzi (1930s mansion, rabbit ravioli), O Vasilis (Melanes), Patatosporos (Agia Anna).
quote: Barozzi Restaurant & Cocktail Bar | Naxos Town | Fine dining in 1930s mansion; rabbit ravioli and sea bass dishes | $$$

claim: Chora dining guide: Doukato reservation essential because it fills every night; To Elliniko zucchini fritters, fried cheese, sea bass.
quote: Doukato - Known for: Naxian cuisine in a courtyard setting - Specialty: Octopus - Reservation: Essential—'fills up every night'

claim: Axiotissa's official site: Greek menu of salads, appetizers, local Naxian cheeses and mains, with an i-host reservations link.
quote: The site includes a reservations link (i-host.gr), suggesting advance bookings are accepted and encouraged.

claim: Named Naxian producers and off-the-beaten-path stops: Kalavros cheese farm (PDO arseniko), Pittaras dairy (Melanes), Makrydimitris organic winery (Glinado, Potamisi/Monemvasia/Assyrtiko), Katerina Galani's galaktoboureko in Halki, Amorginos plate, Axiotissa's owners, Stou Vasilarakiou.
quote: Makrydimitris Winery (Glinado) - Produces: Organic wines from local varieties including Potamisi, Monemvasia, Assyrtiko.

claim: Naxos panigiria run July through September with the odd one in October, including a nine-day Festival of the Virgin Mary in August.
quote: From July through September, with the odd one in October, including a nine-day Festival of the Virgin Mary in August and the Festival of Saint Artemios in October.

claim: Vallindras visits are short (about 5-10 minutes) and seasonal; reviewers report it does not open until April despite listed year-round hours.
quote: The tour takes about 5-10 minutes... it does not open until April although the hours state it is open every day monthly.

claim: Naxos graviera exports are being expanded to about 20 countries by 2026.
quote: the Union plans to increase cheese exports to 20 countries by early 2026

claim: Saint Anna Winery tastings pour 6 to 9 wines with local snacks (olives, cheeses, breadsticks); evening tastings reported to run over two hours, hosted by Emmanuel Petrakis.
quote: The winery serves 6 to 9 different kinds of wines... evening tastings lasting more than two hours covering the history of the vineyards and cellar.

claim: In Naxos high season (July-August) the latest sensible accommodation booking is two weeks before arrival, with one to three months recommended.
quote: when booking in high season, the latest you should book is 2 weeks before arrival, but 1 to 3 months depending on the weeks of your stay are highly recommended
